articles.summary: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths
articles.keyPoints:
• India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths
• Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.
• Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.summary: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.keyPoints:
• The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
• Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.
• The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Tasmac’s Deepavali sales touch ₹441 crore amid POS machine glitches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore

The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) has recorded liquor sales worth ₹441.38 crore during Deepavali 2026. According to sources, on the eve of Deepavali, Tasmac sold liquor worth over ₹234.75 crore and on the day of the festival the sales stood at ₹206.63 crore.

Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore. Salem reported sales of ₹87.52 crore and Coimbatore at ₹70.66 crore. As Monday was a holiday, liquor sales are expected to remain at similar levels (sales of approximately ₹192 crore are expected).

Those tracking the liquor market in Tamil Nadu say sales have dipped marginally this year (Tasmac does not officially disclose its Deepavali sales figures. The data has been collated from various sources for several years).

While some salesmen attributed the dip in sales to machines getting stuck and confusion surrounding the buy back scheme, others said that liquor sales had been unusually high over the past week, with crowds slightly larger than usual. “People were worried that shops might not open because of the issues surrounding the buy back scheme. So, many started stocking up for the festival as early as last week,” said a salesman at a shop in the T. Nagar region.

A senior Tasmac official said that the issues with POS machines would be resolved soon and that around 1,000 new POS machines would be deployed across outlets soon. “Wherever there is a requirement we will deploy these machines.” the official added.
When asked about the issues with POS machines, Minister for Prohibition and Excise K. Vignesh questioned: “The POS machines were working until November 1. What happened after that?”

He also said that around 44 salesmen had been suspended between November 1 and 5 for violating MRP norms. “We have received more complaints of similar violations and will initiate action on them as well,” he added.

Tasmac sources said the corporation is estimated to have collected around ₹38 crore through the Environment Protection Cess. From November 1, 2026, a ₹10 Environmental and Social Welfare Cess was levied on liquor sales to facilitate the buy back of empty bottles. The cess was included in the MRP.

As on July 2026, Tasmac has 4,048 retail vending shops and a workforce of 22,877 (6,473 supervisors, 14,379 salespersons, and 2,025 assistant salespersons). For the year 2025-2026, Tasmac earned a revenue of ₹50,845 crore.

articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

From the poverty income ruler line provided by the recent World Bank estimates, India has recorded one of the fastest extreme income-poverty declines in the world, as per its latest Poverty and Equity brief, which highlights that between 2011 and 2023, an estimated 496 million people moved out of poverty, with extreme income-based poverty ($3/per day) declining to 2.6%.

For the same period, the share of the population living below the lower middle-income country line ($4.20/day, 2021 PPP) fell from 57.7% to 16.1%. Non-monetary poverty indicators, as per OPHI’s Multi-dimensional Poverty Index, also recorded a sharp reduction in overall poverty numbers, i.e., from 53.8% in 2005-06 to 16.4% in 2019-21.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.
• However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Building over Srinagar’s future
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Suspend the FAR and land-use exemptions, along with Section 22, until they are brought within the Master Plan framework and subjected to public objections

Two conversations about the Himalayas are running at the same time, and they are not converging. Everyone agrees that mountain towns are reaching their limits in different ways, springs are drying up, lakes are choking, and slopes are giving way. No hill town should approve large construction before measuring what it can carry. Yet the developmental model is running parallel. Recent notifications and bills in Jammu and Kashmir are making it easier to build more, on more land. Srinagar is being overwhelmed by that.

Let us start with a simple idea. Floor Area Ratio (FAR) determines how much floor space can be built on a plot. On a 100-square-metre plot, an FAR of 200% allows 200 square metres of floor space. When the number is raised, the same plot must hold more people, cars, toilets, drains, etc. Over nine months, the rules have been repeatedly changed. The building by-laws were amended on December 1, 2025. On July 24, 2026, they were extended to Housing Board colonies, with additional FAR and reduced setbacks. On September 9, fresh limits were proposed, including an FAR of 300% for commercial complexes. On September 28, the Ease of Doing Business Bill, 2026, was tabled. In the first week of October, the Lieutenant Governor gave his assent, and the Bill became law.
Political & National Report: Building over Srinagar’s future. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Missing PM2.5 data for several hours on CPCB website understated city’s pollution levels: experts; 227 PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 stations; govt. will look into it: Mishra

Air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with experts warning that the gaps have led to understated pollution levels and resulted in a lower official air quality index (AQI).

According to Dr. D. Saha, former head of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)’s air quality laboratory, AQI values are calculated using a moving or running average of hourly concentrations of eight parameters, including PM2.5 and PM10, over the previous 24 hours.

On Monday (November 9, 2026), PM2.5 data were missing for several hours at many stations in the city, including Anand Vihar, Patparganj and Bawana, on the CPCB website. PM2.5 (particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less in diameter) consists of fine inhalable particles that can penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream, causing respiratory and other diseases. Similar data gaps were reported at several monitoring stations during Deepavali last year as well.

Manoj Kumar, an analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finland-based non-profit research organisation, said the missing hourly PM2.5 data “raised concerns about the assessment of Delhi’s air quality”.

“From midnight on November 8 until 5 a.m. on November 9, 227 hourly PM2.5 observations were missing across 59 CPCB monitoring stations in Delhi. Only 14 stations reported complete data, while the remaining 45 had at least one missing hourly observation,” Mr. Kumar said, adding, “When the hourly PM2.5 data is missing, it will artificially lower the AQI, showing better air quality when the actual air quality is worse.”

When asked about the missing air quality data at several monitoring stations, Delhi Labour Minister Kapil Mishra told the media that the government would look into the issue. The Member Secretary of the CPCB, which releases AQI data, did not respond to calls and messages seeking comment.
Dr. Saha told The Hindu that there should not be gaps in the data, especially during crucial periods.

“If hourly PM2.5 or PM10 value is blank or missing, it will affect the AQI calculated and the final value of the AQI calculated will be less than the actual value of AQI and scientifically incorrect,” Mr. Saha said.

He also said the CPCB had set the measurement range of PM2.5 analysers at 0–1,000 micrograms per cubic metre, which meant they could not measure concentrations above that level. “So, if the value of PM2.5 is beyond 1,000, it should at least be shown as 1,000 instead of showing blank,” he said.

A former DPCC scientist, who did not wish to be identified, said the CPCB recorded PM2.5 values only up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre because there was a minor drop in accuracy at higher levels. “But at very high values, a small drop in accuracy will not matter a lot. Ideally, the CPCB should be measuring the higher values so that we are not missing the peak values,” the official said, adding that not measuring higher concentrations would artificially make air quality appear better.

articles.title: Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India is ready to mediate to establish grain safety agreement for “food corridors”, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy

India is ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish “food corridors”, announced Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcoming the offer after a telephone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of the Ukraine-Russia peace talks set to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Mr. Modi conveyed India’s “readiness” to help with all initiatives to end the nearly five-year-old conflict. The call was followed by another call between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump’s negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, will restart negotiations after three months with Russian and Ukrainian representatives to discuss security guarantees required for a possible ceasefire. The calls from New Delhi came just ahead of the talks in the UAE, and a week before Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the ASEAN-linked summits in Manila. Later this month, Mr. Trump is expected to travel to Shenzhen for the APEC summit in China, that Russian President Vladimir Putin is also expected to attend, making the timing of the Modi-Zelenskyy and Jaishankar-Lavrov calls more significant.

“Prime Minister [Modi] reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy,” the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement about the Modi-Zelenskyy call. “He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict,” it added.

In a post on social media, Mr. Zelenskyy said he had briefed Mr. Modi on the latest developments and stressed that Mr. Modi had said to Mr. Putin that the war must end. The Ukrainian President said Russia must understand that the “global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes” in the Black Sea, and called for India to clarify its peace proposal.

“It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end. Food security could be one such area. We discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” Mr. Zelenskyy wrote.

Within a couple of hours of the announcement, Mr. Jaishankar posted that he had spoken to his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov as well, and said their conversation had “focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives”. Mr. Jaishankar, who has been discussing India’s proposals on a grain export agreement or a food corridor in the Black Sea, on the safety of sea mariners, and safe passage for energy shipments with both countries, had first disclosed the initiatives during a visit to Poland and Ukraine in September. On October 22, during the visit of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to Delhi, Indian officials had said it had reached out to both Russian and Ukrainian governments with a “four-point proposal” for an agreement that would stop attacks on civilians, allow grain and energy exports from both countries through the Black Sea, and end the targeting of ships and seafarers, many of whom are Indian nationals. Highly placed officials had told The Hindu that New Delhi was in close contact with both sides over the specific proposal, and the government had hoped to hear back from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides at the earliest. With talks set to begin on Tuesday, it remains to be seen whether India will join the dialogue already in play with the U.S. and the UAE, or whether New Delhi plans a larger role in mediating or hosting talks between Russia and Ukraine in the future.

articles.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The deceased were identified as a staff nurse and four inmates of a government-recognised children’s home for girls
A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area.

On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned.

Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered.

Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way.

articles.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab.

Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity.
The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1.
Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts.

A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said.
The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone.

In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said.
The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department.
He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue and relief operations during the cyclone.

The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab.

Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity.

The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1.

Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts.

A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said.

The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone.

In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said.

The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department.

He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue and relief operations during the cyclone.

articles.title: Hegseth faces expected U.S. House impeachment vote this week
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday, setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power

Pete Hegseth, the U.S. Defence Secretary, calls himself the Secretary of War, part of his effort to rebrand ‌a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year. Now, with ​a House impeachment vote expected this week, he could soon share something in common with an ⁠actual secretary of war.
William Belknap, who held that title in 1876, became the first, and to date only, civilian leader of the U.S. military to be impeached by Congress.

U.S. Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced articles of impeachment on Monday (November 9, 2026), setting off a two-day ‌clock for an expected House vote on charges including waging war against Iran without congressional approval and other abuses of power.

Congressional sources say the resolution may have the simple majority needed to pass the Republican-controlled ‌House before Democrats take over on January 3. Conviction appears unlikely in the Senate, however, where a two-thirds ‌majority ⁠is required and Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats.
House Speaker Mike Johnson opposed the effort, saying impeachment “in ⁠the middle of hostilities abroad” would be “a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see.”

Voter anger over the war helped Democrats win control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections, intensifying Republican divisions over a conflict that Vice-President J.D. Vance has publicly questioned and Mr. Hegseth has ​defended as “courageous and historic.”

Accused of taking huge kickbacks, ‌Belknap handed President Ulysses Grant his resignation ahead of his scheduled impeachment vote and, according to a Senate history, “burst into tears.” The House impeached him anyway, but the Senate later acquitted him after falling short of the required two-thirds majority.
By contrast, Mr. Hegseth is promising to stay and fight.

Mr. Hegseth has mounted a social media campaign, saying ‌in a defiant video message last week that he would not back down. He also drew a ​comparison to President Donald Trump, who was impeached twice, saying: “It didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”

Asked if he had enough Republican support to defeat the impeachment push, Mr. Hegseth ⁠said on Monday (November 9, 2026): “We’re not worried about that.” He announced a Tuesday (November 10, 2026) press conference, his first at the Pentagon since May.

The case for the Nepalese people needs to be analysed from the prism of climate litigations used by plaintiffs in many jurisdictions of Europe and the U.S. in the last two decades.

articles.title: Return of patriarch: Farooq steps in as NC old guard reasserts influence to check Omar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In seven decades of the National Conference, the parallel party meeting was seen as a rare implosion and a visible crack that the Opposition parties could exploit to tilt the balance of numbers against the Omar Abdullah government.

The stand-off between the 17 MLAs of the ruling National Conference (NC) and Kashmir’s first political family, the Abdullahs, has had a rare consequence. It has brought the 89-year-old party patriarch, Farooq Abdullah, back into the saddle to steer the party and shape how the government functions, after he had nearly faded from affairs run entirely by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah.

The stalemate began on October 27 with the CM’s Cabinet reshuffle, after which at least three senior party leaders publicly expressed resentment over not being inducted. Later that day, the disgruntled legislators held a meeting, conspicuously in the absence of the Abdullahs, and subsequently submitted a charter of demands to the party leadership, which included intensifying the struggle for the restoration of Statehood and special status, removing Nasir Aslam Wani as the CM’s Adviser and reassigning the Roads and Buildings portfolio, currently held by Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary.

articles.title: Kochi Corporation plans water security assessment to strengthen city’s resilience
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority, is expected to be completed in six months
A water security assessment project is being planned for the Kochi Corporation to strengthen the city’s water resilience.

The multipronged project, being developed by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Palakkad, will address issues, including water scarcity and pollution, besides focussing on canal rejuvenation, sewage management, and flood mitigation. The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority (KWA), is expected to be completed in six months.

Once completed, the project is expected to provide a comprehensive framework to guide the planning and implementation of water security projects in the city, said Athira P., associate professor, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Palakkad.

“Different parts of Kochi face specific issues, be it frequently interrupted water supply, flooding, pollution or an increase in the reporting of water-borne diseases. Water security in a region is assessed based on aspects such as water quality and quantity, water-related disasters and ecological factors. A multidimensional assessment is being planned,” said Ms. Athira.

The findings will be compiled into a dynamic model designed to help administrators, incorporating projections for the coming years. These projections will help identify the interventions required over the next 10 to 15 years, as climate and land-use patterns are expected to change in the city.

“The data will help identify the specific issues affecting different divisions of the Corporation. This will help formulate projects more effectively and identify the interventions required,” said Ms. Athira.
“Such an assessment assumes significance as several parts of the city face challenges such as pollution, water scarcity and saltwater intrusion,” the sources added.

articles.title: Demand grows for alternative greenfield road corridors to Infopark in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: IT professionals flag safety concerns over narrow, potholed roads and traffic snarls, and call for parallel roads through vacant plots to improve connectivity to Infopark

Close on the heels of a decision to widen roads around the collectorate and to convert IMG Junction-Infopark road into a one-way corridor, IT professionals and others have demanded alternative greenfield road corridors to reach Infopark.

Around one lakh IT employees and innumerable others now commute along mostly congested roads to reach the IT hub. Pratidhwani, a welfare organisation of IT professionals that has been spearheading the demand for better road connectivity and public transport to Infopark, highlighted safety concerns arising from narrow, potholed roads and reckless driving by buses in Kochi and its suburbs.
This comes in the wake of a young woman getting killed after a speeding private bus rammed her at a narrow, footpath-less stretch on Infopark road on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

“It is high time the Thrikkakara municipality, Public Works department, Kerala Road Fund Board, traffic police, and other agencies concerned woke up from their slumber, as IT professionals and others have been having a harrowing time over the past decade due to narrow roads and traffic snarls. This is particularly true of the Collectorate Junction-Infopark road and the Pallikkara-Athani road, where traffic congestion is acute. With buildings having come up on either side of these roads, parallel roads should be built through vacant plots. This will help convert many existing roads into one-way corridors. In addition, IMG Junction must be redesigned and a roundabout built, for which minimal land acquisition would be required. Overbridges or flyovers could also be built to bypass bottlenecked junctions,” said Jidheesh Rajan of Pratidhwani.
The aim is to rope in like-minded people and organisations in the matter. Apart from approaching the court, follow-up action would be taken in the form of campaigns, he added.

Sajan John, former chief operating officer of Kochi Water Metro Limited, sought the urgent intervention of government agencies to address traffic congestion and chaos on the 1.50-km-long IMG Junction-Infopark Carnival Junction corridor, which is used by tens of thousands of people daily, including by approximately 1 lakh Infopark employees. Similar is the plight of Kakkanad-Pallikara road and Athani Junction. In both corridors, vast tracts of vacant land are available behind buildings facing the road, and two-lane roads can be built parallel to the existing ones.

Welcoming a proposal to convert roads around the collectorate building as one-way corridors, Mr. John called for a comprehensive traffic re-arrangement plan in the IMG Junction-Signal Junction-Padamugal-NGO Quarters-Olimugal Junction corridor.

articles.title: Trinamool MLA Paresh Ram Das arrested on charges of rape and extortion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several leaders of the Trinamool Congress have been arrested after the BJP came to power in May 2026, which includes five former Ministers

Mamata All India Trinamool Congress MLA Paresh Ram Das was arrested on Monday (November 9, 2026) from Kolkata’s Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. Police said there were several charges against the Canning Paschim MLA including extortion and rape.

According to police sources, the Special Operations Group (SOG) of Baruipur district police began tracking the MLA after receiving information that he was heading to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport. articles.title: Outcry as J&K Bank implements reservation policy pushed by ex-chairman and VHP trustee R.K. Chhibber
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The bank has decided to fill 1400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy

The amended reservation policy of the J&K Bank, which was introduced by ex-chairman R.K. Chhibber in 2021-2022, who was later appointed as a Trustee of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), on Monday (November 9, 2026) triggered a political storm with regional political parties, religious and social organisations opposing it, with many terming it “an act of exclusion in the garb of reservation”.

For the first time, the J&K Bank, which provides high-end jobs in a region with a low corporate footprint, is facing a push from the regional parties, including the ruling National Conference (NC). The bank has decided to fill 1400 vacancies, including 323 probationary officers and 1033 posts for banking associates, as per the new reservation policy. It also reduced the age limit from 32 to 30 for the Open Merit and increased the age criteria for the reserved categories to 40 years.

“The existing upper age limit of 30 years needed reconsideration. The recruitment age limit should be raised to 40 years to provide more opportunities to eligible aspirants,” said J&K Education Minister Shamima Firdous.

The J&K Bank is considered one of the main non-government recruitment agencies of the Union Territory (UT). Around 1.40 lakh locals had applied for 1500 banking associates in 2021-2022 during the tenure of Mr. Chhibber, who later faced allegations of regional imbalance with more candidates selected from the Jammu region against the aspirants from the Kashmir division. In spite of being selected as a trustee of the VHP, Mr. Chhibber continued to be on the Board of Directors till 2026 and remained a key proponent for introducing the new reservation policy.

According to the notification, the bank has decided to open positions to 60% for the reserved categories and 40% for the Open Merit. The reservation policy adopted by the bank recruitment included 8% from the Schedule Caste, 20% from the Schedule Tribe, 8% from the Other Backward Classes, 4% from the Actual Line of Control/International Border, 10 % from the Resident of Backward Area (RBA)and 10% from the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).

The J&K Students Association (JKSA) sought intervention of J&K Lieutenant-Governor into the matter. “Only approximately 542 posts fall under Open Merit, while the remaining vacancies are allocated to reserved categories. Merit should remain the cornerstone of recruitment and every eligible candidate must have a fair opportunity to compete. The educated youth of J&K have already endured years of uncertainty and limited employment opportunities. They should not be penalised for circumstances over which they had no control,” reads the letter written by Zubair Reshi, national spokesperson of the JKSA, addressed to the L-G.

The letter demanded that the concerns surrounding the availability of opportunities, equitable representation and the overall recruitment framework “deserve careful examination by the competent authorities”. It pointed out that the bank announcement of fresh recruitment came “after a prolonged gap of nearly six years”.

“The upper age limit has caused widespread disappointment among aspirants. Thousands of young people have invested years of their lives, considerable financial resources and immense effort in preparing for competitive examinations,” it added.

Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) legislator Waheed ur Rehman Parra termed the bank recruitment policy “a concern”. “It’s deeply concerning. The age limit at 20-30 years is completely unfair to thousands of overaged aspirants who have been waiting patiently for years. Applying reservation policies in a commercial institution like J&K Bank undermines meritocracy for our local youth. Revoke reservation in the recruitment. Give our educated youth a fair and equal chance,” said Mr. Parra.

CPI(M) leader has backed the demands of the students. “The government has set the recruitment age at 40 years. Given the rising unemployment in J&K, I request the J&K Bank authorities to reconsider the age criteria and raise the upper age limit, thereby providing an opportunity to more deserving and eligible candidates,” CPI(M) leader M.Y. Tarigami.

articles.title: El Nino Watch: the impacts around the world this week
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Experts say it could help make 2027 the hottest year on record

An exceptionally strong El Nino is driving weather disruptions around the globe, stoking food security fears and increasing the chances that 2026 will be the second-hottest year on record, experts say.
Here is how the climate phenomenon has been playing out around the world in the last week.

The world is on track for 2026 to be the second-hottest year on record, with the El Nino weather pattern turbocharging human-driven global warming, the European Union’s climate monitor said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

“October has continued the pattern of remarkable global warmth, with record global and surface ocean temperatures,” said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which operates the Copernicus monitor.
“An exceptionally strong El Nino is adding further heat to a climate already warmed by human activities,” she said.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming.
Experts say it could help make 2027 the hottest year on record.
Peru declared a state of emergency across much of the country on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), given the “imminent danger” posed by El Nino-linked flooding, authorities said.
It followed Bolivia’s decision to announce a national state of emergency over the weather pattern’s effects.
El Nino cycles can bring heavy rain to Latin America, and downpours have already inundated parts of Peru’s northern Tumbes and Piura regions.

Experts say it could help make 2027 the hottest year on record

An exceptionally strong El Nino is driving weather disruptions around the globe, stoking food security fears and increasing the chances that 2026 will be the second-hottest year on record, experts say.

Here is how the climate phenomenon has been playing out around the world in the last week.

The world is on track for 2026 to be the second-hottest year on record, with the El Nino weather pattern turbocharging human-driven global warming, the European Union’s climate monitor said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

“October has continued the pattern of remarkable global warmth, with record global and surface ocean temperatures,” said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which operates the Copernicus monitor.

“An exceptionally strong El Nino is adding further heat to a climate already warmed by human activities,” she said.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming.

Experts say it could help make 2027 the hottest year on record.

Peru declared a state of emergency across much of the country on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), given the “imminent danger” posed by El Nino-linked flooding, authorities said.

It followed Bolivia’s decision to announce a national state of emergency over the weather pattern’s effects.

El Nino cycles can bring heavy rain to Latin America, and downpours have already inundated parts of Peru’s northern Tumbes and Piura regions.

articles.title: Heat-trapping carbon pollution drops, but scientists cite Iran war rather than energy progress
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In 2026, the world emitted 42.2 billion tonne of heat-trapping carbon dioxide from the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas. It's a 0.4% decrease from last year, according to the scientists of the Global Carbon Project

Global carbon pollution dropped this year ever so slightly, but it's more because of oil shocks reverberating from the Iran war than anything the world has done to fight climate change, scientists said in a new study.

In 2026, the world emitted 42.2 billion tonne of heat-trapping carbon dioxide from the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas. It's a 0.4% decrease from last year, according to the scientists of the Global Carbon Project, which publishes its estimates in the journal Earth System Science Data Discussions .

“It's downwards which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz,” said study co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway. “So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.”
The war in Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping artery for petroleum products, pushing up global prices of gasoline and oil.
They found oil emissions dropped nearly 2% and natural gas fell 0.3%, while coal was up 0.6%.

The international team of more than 140 scientists use data from around the world to calculate the yearly emissions figure, with estimates for the last few months of the year, and then present them at the UN climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkey. Peters said they are certain that this was related to the war-triggered energy shocks because of both the timing and type of fuel emission drops.

If the overall carbon dioxide emission drop were due solely to a rise in renewables and a systemic drop in fossil fuel use, oil emissions “would slowly come up to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, whereas what we see this year is oil emissions are going up and then suddenly BANG, down 2 per cent,” Peters said.
This is the third time global carbon pollution dropped in the 21st century. The other two times were because of the global recession in 2009 and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
In those past two crises, people hoped the recovery from the shocks would emphasise clean energy, Peters said, "but at the end of the day, we seem to go back to where we were before.”
Outside experts greeted the figures with a mix of hope and skepticism that it will last.

articles.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The sudden emergence of Nvidia CEO Huang's infidelity has created concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence

U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday (November 9, 2026) that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
“I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape,” Mr. Trump said at a White House briefing.

The sudden emergence of Mr. Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence.

Mr. Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Mr. Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Mr. Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

Mr. Huang -- a singular figure in the technology landscape and one of the world's wealthiest people -- has acknowledged that he had an affair, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.

“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security,” Mr. Huang said in his letter.
Nvidia announced Sunday (November 8, 2026) it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Mr. Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The episode is also attracting congressional scrutiny, with top Democrats Sen. Mark Warner and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries saying on Monday (November 9, 2026) that they are interested in investigating it further. Jeffries said the Nvidia issue came up during a closed-door session with the CIA director and the Director of National Intelligence that was primarily about Iran.

“We're going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened,” he said, “and what the implications are in terms of America's national security.”

articles.title: Pope meets survivors of clergy abuse in Argentina as it reckons with legacy and ongoing cases
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Vatican said Pope Leo spent about an hour meeting individually, and then as a group, with five victims of abuse by clergy and “church institutions” who were chosen by the local church

Pope Leo XIV met survivors of clergy abuse on Monday (November 9, 2026) during his visit to Argentina, a country that has been reckoning with the Catholic Church's legacy of sex abuse and cover-up, including in cases in which the Argentine Pope Francis intervened.

The Vatican said Pope Leo spent about an hour meeting individually, and then as a group, with five victims of abuse by clergy and “church institutions” who were chosen by the local church. The meeting took place before Pope Leo left for an event at the Catholic University of Argentina.
Pope Leo listened to their “painful stories and proposals to consolidate paths of healing in the church,” said a statement from Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni.

Acknowledging that there were other groups of victims who had wanted to meet with Pope Leo, “the pope expressed his closeness and desire to reinforce paths of protection, of welcome and accompaniment in the church,” it said.

Victims groups had said they wanted to meet with Pope Leo and were denied, including a group of 43 women who allege they were subjected to human trafficking and forced labour at centres of the conservative group Opus Dei in Argentina.

Their allegations implicate senior members of Opus, some of whom have been formally accused in a criminal investigation into the women's claims. Prosecutors have requested that the members be summoned for questioning, but the judge has not ordered it. Opus has denied wrongdoing.

Given the ongoing criminal investigation, it is perhaps unlikely that Pope Leo would have intervened by meeting with them in this case. However, in general, the American pope has followed in the footsteps of Francis and to a lesser extent Pope Benedict XVI by meeting with abuse survivors on his foreign trips, and another meeting is expected after he arrives later this week in Peru.

Ahead of the Argentine visit, survivors had also demanded stronger action from the Vatican against those accused or convicted in criminal courts but whose fates within the church's internal legal processes haven't been made public.

Survivors' groups have cited several high-profile priests convicted of serious crimes, including Julio Grassi and former Bishop Gustavo Zanchetta. Francis intervened in both cases in favour of the priests who were subsequently convicted by criminal courts.

Grassi, once a prominent figure who ran homes for orphaned children, is serving a 15-year sentence for sexually abusing a minor. Francis, who at the time was still Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio and the archbishop of Buenos Aires, in 2010 commissioned a four-volume, 2,000-plus-page forensic study of Grassi's case that concluded he was innocent, that his victims were lying and that the case never should have gone to trial.

articles.title: Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinised after foreign intelligence concerns
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley

U.S. President Donald Trump’s close relationship with embattled ‌Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday (November 9, 2026), after the company ​said its board was investigating whether the tech executive has been the target ⁠of a foreign intelligence effort.

Mr. Huang is one of Mr. Trump’s closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates to at least 2025. Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support ‌for the administration’s agenda and become a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.
Advanced chips are the backbone of ‌the U.S. AI boom and government officials have previously tried to restrict China’s access to ‌them ⁠through export controls to stifle its AI capabilities.

Nvidia’s board launched its probe after ⁠a New York Times report said Mr. Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials believe passed information to the Chinese government. Nvidia shares hit a seven-month low on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. Huang has a direct line to the ​president. A Reuters reporter saw Huang’s full ‌name pop up on Mr. Trump’s phone in December 2025.

Mr. Huang flew with Mr. Trump to China on Air Force One in May, the first visit by a U.S. president to China in nearly a decade. Mr. Huang attended a high-profile state dinner in September for Chinese President ‌Xi Jinping at the White House. The company committed $25 million for Mr. Trump’s planned ​White House ballroom, according to media reports.

The New York Times reported that Mr. Trump was briefed on Mr. Huang’s relationship with the woman and that she was giving information ⁠to the Chinese government, and chose not to act on the information.
Neither the White House nor Nvidia’s communications team immediately responded to a Reuters request for comment on their relationship.

“I’m pushing to investigate ‌Jensen Huang and Nvidia to determine whether our national security was compromised,” said Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, in a post on X. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration, who’s making these decisions, and who’s really got their hand on the wheel.”

Mr. Huang’s relationship with Mr. Trump has coincided with several favourable policy developments for the company. In April 2025, the administration backed off plans to restrict exports of certain Nvidia AI chips to China ‌after Mr. Huang attended a dinner at Mr. Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.

In an advisory dated November 5, 2026, published on its website on November 6, the medical regulator said it had come across instances of institutions purportedly offering medical and allied health courses without obtaining the requisite permission from competent authorities.

The advisory warns that misleading advertisements, websites, social media promotions, unauthorised admission offers and false representations by institutions or agents could leave students and their families vulnerable to fraud. It asks prospective students to verify the authenticity of the institution, the course being offered, the approved intake and the permission granted for the relevant academic year.

articles.title: Why is rural internet connectivity hard to expand? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The past few years have seen a major, but not total, reduction in the lack of internet connectivity in rural areas. Why is it hard to make access more universal?

The story so far: According to data received by The Hindu under the RTI Act, 2005, the number of villages without 4G access in the last four years has declined by three-fourths, a result of a scheme by BSNL to “saturate” all uncovered villages with 4G access. Meanwhile, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has yet to finish procedures to approve any satellite internet provider, which would theoretically bring the number of such villages down to zero.

As such, telecom operators and internet service providers have to spend enormous amounts of money to reach an exceedingly small number of users. Building fiber out to villages, and then setting up phone towers there, is prohibitively expensive, if operators are only guided in their economics by the number of users that such efforts eventually reach.

articles.title: Mystery of a missing sewage treatment plant tells the tale of the lake in Krishnakanth Park
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Currently restricted to about three acres and divided into three separate ponds with interconnecting canals, the water body is now set to be increased to 12 acres

The lake inside the Krishnakath Park in Yousufguda has come a full circle over the past two decades, before the recent announcement by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Development Agency (HYDRAA) revealing plans to develop and restore the lake.

HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath is taking special interest in expansion of the lake by four times its existing size, in order to impound the storm water that inundates Ameerpet and surrounding localities downstream every time it rains.
Currently restricted to about three acres and divided into three separate ponds with interconnecting canals, the water body is now set to be increased to 12 acres.
Work to fell and translocate trees from the park is already underway, with 34 trees marked for felling and 156 for translocation.

This initiative will largely reduce the 22-acre park space and drown its lawns, trees, gazebos and other facilities originally established 22 years ago. The project pivots on the argument that the entire park stands on what was originally a lake.

The lake, in fact, is a textbook example of how governments squander public money with no attention to sustainability or accountability. A simple search for a sewage treatment plant which has disappeared over the years lays bare the whole story.

The Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) was first established way back in 2003-04, with the intention of filling the three ponds constructed as part of the park’s development. The park was launched in 2004, by the then chief minister of the joint state of Andhra Pradesh, N. Chandrababu Naidu.

“There was no lake. Before the park, it was a colossal garbage dump. We got down to the daunting task of clearing all the trash in order to build a beautiful park there. Digging very deep, we built strong gazebos with granite, despite objections that the foundations would be at risk due to enormous amounts of rubble underneath. The three ponds were built so as to provide water for the greenery,” shared N. Chandramohan Reddy, who was then the Director, Urban Forestry, of Hyderabad Municipal Corporation.
Ramaraju, a senior citizen from Kalyan Nagar remembers a huge 22-acre lake at the location which had actually provided water for the crops.

“There was this heavy cascade of water that flowed from the lake through Madhura Nagar, and I remember seeing paddy fields on both sides during 1980s. Eventually with city development, sewage and industrial waste started flowing into the lake, and later it was turned into garbage dump,” Mr. Ramaraju reminisced.

articles.title: CSIR-CCMB team identifies potential new targets to fight Tuberculosis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains

A team of scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) has identified critical weaknesses in the bacterium that causes Tuberculosis (TB), a finding that could pave the way for the development of new treatments against one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases.

The discovery is particularly significant for India, which accounts for nearly a quarter of global TB cases and about a third of drug-resistant infections, according to the World Health Organisation’s Global TB Report 2025 . Drug-resistant TB remains a major public health challenge, as treatment requires a combination of antibiotics taken over several months and is becoming increasingly difficult due to the emergence of resistant strains.

Led by CCMB Director Vinay Kumar Nandicoori, the research team mapped the protein export machinery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the bacterium responsible for TB. The study sheds light on how the pathogen transports proteins within and outside its cells, a process essential for its growth, survival and ability to cause disease.

The research was carried out by joint first authors Priyadarshini Sanyal and Jagadeeshwari Uppada in collaboration with scientists from the Institute of Mathematical Sciences, Chennai, led by Areejit Samal, and the Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad.

Using a combination of computational modelling and laboratory experiments, the researchers identified 92 key components and nearly 200 molecular reactions involved in the bacterium’s protein transport network. These included the general Sec pathway, the Twin-Arginine Translocation (Tat) system and the specialised ESX secretion systems unique to this group of bacteria.

“Protein secretion acts like a delivery system inside the bacterium and is vital for its survival,” said Dr Uppada. The team focused on two major secretion pathways, SecA1 and Tat, employing CRISPR-based gene-silencing technology to reduce their activity. The results were striking: bacterial growth declined sharply both in laboratory cultures and inside immune cells, demonstrating that both pathways are essential for the pathogen’s survival.

Dr Priyadarshini Sanyal said further analysis revealed that disrupting these systems affected the export of more than 100 proteins in the SecA1 pathway and around 140 proteins linked to the Tat system. Researchers also observed structural damage to the bacterial cell membrane, making it unstable and more permeable. Proteins that normally remain inside the bacterium began leaking into the surrounding environment.

Dr Nandicoori said that these changes highlight the close connection between protein secretion and the maintenance of the bacterial cell envelope, a key factor behind TB’s persistence and resistance to treatment. The findings, published in the peer-reviewed journal Molecular & Cellular Proteomics , could help researchers identify new drug targets, although translating the discovery into effective medicines will require several more years of research.

articles.title: Prashant Kishor’s Brahminical criticism of BJP’s Hindutva
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Jan Suraaj party founder urges Brahmins in Bihar’s Mithila to rethink BJP Hindutva, linking secularism, social justice, and Muslim-OBC political coalitions

Secularism is a modern, constitutional principle. In real-world politics, the manifestation of this principle is tested against a rather narrow yardstick: the fair representation of religious minorities, particularly Muslims. Generally speaking, the English-speaking secularists are unaware of the caste dynamics that come into play in the field operation of representative politics, and they are also resistant to the idea of discussing caste as a determinant.

The intersection of caste representation and religious representation can be framed as an intersection of social justice and secularism in electoral politics. The caste dynamics of politics are often manifested as critiques by non-Brahmins against Brahminism. A Brahmin perspective on these dynamics is rare, and that is the reason why Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor’s address to fellow Brahmins in Bihar ’s Mithila region is an extremely valuable opportunity to peer into the emerging thinking within the community. He said BJP’s Hindu communalism, which excludes Muslims from electoral calculations, has cost the Brahmins heavily and asked them to rethink their position.

articles.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket fridges
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of France’s supermarkets

France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's massive cyberattack on supermarket fridges , summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions against those responsible for the attack.

The October 12 attack sent refrigerator temperatures soaring, affecting about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets. In a statement Monday, prosecutors in Paris said they found that Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard was behind the large-scale cyberattack.

The French Foreign Ministry condemned the attack “in the strongest possible terms,” and French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, speaking on the sidelines of G7 talks in Paris, said the Iranian ambassador was being summoned to “strongly protest against this extremely serious act.”

“This is an attack of unprecedented scale and aggressiveness,” Mr. Barrot said. “It is the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage on French soil, and it represents a major threat to our national interests and the security of the French people. That is why it will not go unanswered.”
“We will impose sanctions at the European level against all those responsible for this attack,” he added, vowing to take “any other measures needed” to respond to it and deter future attacks.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said in a statement that a formal judicial investigation was opened Monday into suspected organised cybercrime with the aggravating circumstance of “having been committed to serve the interests of a foreign power — in this case, Iran."

The investigation targets Shahid Kaveh, the leader of an Iranian group described as a “cyber unit” affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, as well as his two deputies and any other individuals who might be identified in connection with the case.

Investigators found that the attackers had used Farsi and IP addresses linked to devices located in Iran, Mr. Beccuau said. The Paris prosecutor's office is seeking international arrest warrants, she said.

In the early hours of October 12, attackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France. Temperatures reached 50 degrees Celsius for about six hours, forcing stores to discard fresh and frozen goods. The Intermarche supermarket chain reported losses of “tens of millions of euros” in a single day.

articles.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship

Nvidia ​and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued on ‌Monday (November 9, 2026) in a proposed class action accusing ​them of defrauding shareholders by ⁠concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

According to a complaint filed in federal court ‌in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Huang's alleged affair with ‌Alice Huang, a former executive ‌of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed who is not related to ⁠him, and did not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened Nvidia's reputation and ​business prospects.
The New ‌York Times reported last month about the alleged relationship, and that U.S. authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence ‌asset.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment.
Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship.

He co-founded Nvidia and ‌has led the Santa Clara, California-based company as it became the world's most valuable chipmaker and made him one of the world's most prominent symbols of the artificial intelligence boom.

Nvidia announced a probe into ‌the matter on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Its shares closed down ​4.3% on Monday (November 9, 2026), reducing Nvidia's market capitalisation by approximately $190 billion. The lawsuit ⁠was filed five minutes after the U.S. stock ⁠market closed.
It is common for shareholders to sue companies after unexpected share ‌price declines. Nvidia shareholders, led by Mark Kistenmacher are seeking unspecified damages from ​the defendants.
