articles.title: At 1,152, Punjab records season’s biggest single-day jump in farm fires on Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice
Punjab witnessed its sharpest single-day spike in paddy stubble-burning incidents this season on Deepavali, with 1,152 farm fires reported across the State, according to official data.
This pushed the State's total count from 3,307 on November 7 to 4,459 on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The highest number of farm fires this season has been reported from Tarn Taran at 654, the data showed.
The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice.
The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1.

With 194 fires, Sangrur recorded the highest number of stubble-burning incidents on Sunday (November 8), taking its seasonal tally to 488. Ferozepur reported 157 incidents, bringing its total to 592; and Bathinda added 132 cases, taking its count to 406.
Patiala recorded 92 fresh farm fires, raising its cumulative tally to 288. Barnala reported 91 new incidents and Ludhiana 71.

The data showed that till Sunday (November 8), enforcement agencies had registered 884 FIRs under Section 223 (disobedience of orders promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and marked 1,017 red entries in land revenue records against farmers found burning stubble.
Fines totalling over ₹62 lakh have been imposed as environmental compensation in 1,228 cases of stubble burning, with over ₹32 lakh already recovered.

Recently, taking a serious view of the "very high" number of farm fires in Punjab, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) held a meeting with senior bureaucrats and police officers from 12 districts to review steps to prevent stubble burning.

The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice

Punjab witnessed its sharpest single-day spike in paddy stubble-burning incidents this season on Deepavali, with 1,152 farm fires reported across the State, according to official data.

This pushed the State's total count from 3,307 on November 7 to 4,459 on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The highest number of farm fires this season has been reported from Tarn Taran at 654, the data showed.

The latest figures indicate a significant rise in crop residue burning despite government advisories, enforcement measures and monetary penalties aimed at discouraging the practice.

The annual farm fire monitoring period begins on September 15, two weeks before paddy procurement starts on October 1.

With 194 fires, Sangrur recorded the highest number of stubble-burning incidents on Sunday (November 8), taking its seasonal tally to 488. Ferozepur reported 157 incidents, bringing its total to 592; and Bathinda added 132 cases, taking its count to 406.

Patiala recorded 92 fresh farm fires, raising its cumulative tally to 288. Barnala reported 91 new incidents and Ludhiana 71.

The data showed that till Sunday (November 8), enforcement agencies had registered 884 FIRs under Section 223 (disobedience of orders promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and marked 1,017 red entries in land revenue records against farmers found burning stubble.

Fines totalling over ₹62 lakh have been imposed as environmental compensation in 1,228 cases of stubble burning, with over ₹32 lakh already recovered.

Recently, taking a serious view of the "very high" number of farm fires in Punjab, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) held a meeting with senior bureaucrats and police officers from 12 districts to review steps to prevent stubble burning.

articles.title: Raptadu chainsaw attack victim’s condition improving, says A.P. Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dressing has been changed for injuries on her head, neck, face, arms, and back. The wounds are healing well and she is responding positively to the treatment, says Satya Kumar Yadav

Minister of Health Satya Kumar Yadav on Monday (November 9, 2026) said that the health condition of M. Gopika, who was injured in the chainsaw attack by a youth at Raptadu ZPHS, has improved further. The girl is currently undergoing treatment at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru.

In an official statement here on the health condition of Gopika, the Minister said that the girl was shifted to a general ward and the medical team has changed the dressings on her wounds once again. “Dressing has been changed for injuries on her head, neck, face, arms, and back. The wounds are healing well. Gopika has responded positively to the treatment,” the Minister said.

Mr. Satya Kumar Yadav further said that the splint on her left arm has been removed, allowing for better movement of the limb. Gopika is experiencing chest pain when coughing and it is being managed with medication.
As the oral food intake is low currently, Gopika is being fed with the help of a nasogastric tube. The Minister said that the doctors are encouraging the girl to start consuming food orally.

Earlier in the day, HRD Minister Nara Lokesh who has been monitoring the girl’s health posted on X, “The plastic surgery team completed her wound debridement and suture adjustments today without any complications. Her wounds are healing well, and she tolerated the procedure extremely well. An encouraging step forward - the team removed her left-hand sling so she can begin moving her arm again! While she remains on round-the-clock pain management and feeding support, she is stable and being prepared to move from the PICU to the ward under expert care. Keeping her in our prayers.”

articles.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab.

Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity.
The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1.
Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts.

A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said.
The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone.

In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said.
The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department.
He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue and relief operations during the cyclone.

articles.title: Children make up for half of Deepavali eye-injury cases at Hyderabad hospital
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Doctors say most patients were treated without surgery, but 10 individuals require surgical intervention, while bystanders also accounted for numerous injuries from a range of fireworks, underscoring the festival’s risk to ocular health

Nine-year-old Mokshit was among 15 patients admitted to the Burns Ward of the government-run Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital in Hyderabad following eye injuries during Deepavali celebrations. Brought all the way from Bhadrachalam, the boy was anxiously waiting for doctors to decide whether he needed surgery after a firecracker fragment struck his eye.

“My son was bursting a firecracker when suddenly a part of it flew off and hit his eye. My husband and I took him to a local hospital in Bhadrachalam, where the doctors said he might require surgery and advised us to bring him here. We are now waiting for the doctors to examine him and decide on the further course of treatment,” said Lakshmi, the boy’s mother.

Mokshit’s case is among several involving children, who accounted for half of the patients treated for firecracker-related eye injuries during Deepavali at the hospital. In sheer numbers, of the 87 patients who reported to Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital over November 7 and 8, a total of 37 were children.

Hospital superintendent Modini Pandharpurkar said 54 patients were treated during the corresponding period last year. She expects the numbers to rise over the next two to three days as more patients from districts are likely to reach Hyderabad for treatment.

Of the 15 patients admitted, 10 were scheduled to undergo surgery on Monday. Two adult patients had a poor prognosis while one child was expected to recover, according to the latest hospital update. One patient was referred to Osmania General Hospital (OGH) and three to Niloufer Hospital for further treatment. Two others were under observation, while the two more admitted on Monday were still being evaluated, Dr. Pandharpurkar said.

She pointed out that several patients were bystanders who sustained injuries while walking on roads or standing near places where firecrackers were being burst. Bullet bombs, mirchi bombs and rockets were among the firecrackers linked to the injuries reported this year.

Meanwhile, the L.V. Prasad Eye Institute (LVPEI) reported 92 firecracker-related injuries over the two nights of Deepavali celebrations. Its emergency report for November 7 recorded two firecracker injury cases between 7 p.m, and 7 a.m., apart from 14 other emergency cases.

The number surged on November 8, the day of Deepavali, with the hospital treating 90 patients for firecracker-related injuries between 7 p.m. and 5 a.m. One other emergency case was also reported during this period.
Of those 90 patients, 25 were advised surgery, with 22 procedures planned. Six surgeries had been performed, according to the hospital’s emergency report.

articles.title: Police seize third video allegedly showing ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani abusing minor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The deleted content was retrieved by cyber forensic experts from a storage device, say police sources

The Greater Chennai Police have seized one more video purportedly showing Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani sexually abusing a minor girl, taking the total number of such videos recovered in the case to three, police sources said on Monday.

The deleted video, believed to have been recorded a few years ago, was retrieved by cyber forensic experts from a storage device seized from the premises of Shanthi, a close associate of Veeramani. “The video shows the octogenarian businessman in a compromising position with a minor. We suspect that Shanthi recorded the visuals and subsequently deleted them,” a police officer said.

Investigators are in the process of identifying the victim in the video. “This is the third video seized in the case and there could be more. With this fresh evidence and a witness in another case of child abuse coming forward as a complainant, the total number of victims has risen to 13,” the officer said. Besides Veeramani, Shanthi and her husband Mahendra Simhan, six other accused persons have so far been arrested in eight different cases and lodged in the Puzhal Central Prison.

Police sources said the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) and the Income Tax Department had been alerted about suspicious financial transactions detected during the investigation in the cases of alleged sexual abuse of minors involving Veeramani. The businessman and his close associates are facing seven cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and a case relating to the abetment of the suicide of a minor in 2004.

During the course of investigation, police uncovered substantial financial transactions between the Gem Group of Companies, owned by Veeramani, and a private individual, Prakash Kanniah. Investigators subsequently froze the latter’s bank accounts, which reportedly held several crores of rupees, the sources said.

Further inquiries revealed that gold bars weighing more than 20 kg had been purchased and delivered at a couple of locations in the city. However, the police could not trace the gold during searches conducted on the premises of the accused persons.
The transactions reportedly took place around the time Veeramani sold two parcels of land along the East Coast Road for a total consideration of about ₹80 crore, the sources said.

The deleted content was retrieved by cyber forensic experts from a storage device, say police sources

The Greater Chennai Police have seized one more video purportedly showing Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani sexually abusing a minor girl, taking the total number of such videos recovered in the case to three, police sources said on Monday.

The deleted video, believed to have been recorded a few years ago, was retrieved by cyber forensic experts from a storage device seized from the premises of Shanthi, a close associate of Veeramani. “The video shows the octogenarian businessman in a compromising position with a minor. We suspect that Shanthi recorded the visuals and subsequently deleted them,” a police officer said.

Investigators are in the process of identifying the victim in the video. “This is the third video seized in the case and there could be more. With this fresh evidence and a witness in another case of child abuse coming forward as a complainant, the total number of victims has risen to 13,” the officer said. Besides Veeramani, Shanthi and her husband Mahendra Simhan, six other accused persons have so far been arrested in eight different cases and lodged in the Puzhal Central Prison.

Police sources said the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) and the Income Tax Department had been alerted about suspicious financial transactions detected during the investigation in the cases of alleged sexual abuse of minors involving Veeramani. The businessman and his close associates are facing seven cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and a case relating to the abetment of the suicide of a minor in 2004.

During the course of investigation, police uncovered substantial financial transactions between the Gem Group of Companies, owned by Veeramani, and a private individual, Prakash Kanniah. Investigators subsequently froze the latter’s bank accounts, which reportedly held several crores of rupees, the sources said.

Further inquiries revealed that gold bars weighing more than 20 kg had been purchased and delivered at a couple of locations in the city. However, the police could not trace the gold during searches conducted on the premises of the accused persons.

The transactions reportedly took place around the time Veeramani sold two parcels of land along the East Coast Road for a total consideration of about ₹80 crore, the sources said.

The transfer of substantial money to an individual projected as an adviser to the companies and the purchase of gold bars have come under scrutiny amid allegations that certain persons had used their influence to help Veeramani and his associates evade legal action despite a specific complaint of sexual abuse of a minor against them.

Questioning Prakash Kanniah who is said to be absconding and believed to be staying in the United Kingdom could throw more light on the transactions, the sources said.

“We suspect that money or gold could have changed hands as part of the larger conspiracy to help the accused persons. Hence, we intimated the ED and the Income Tax Department about the suspicious transactions,” the officer, who did not want to be quoted, said.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Deadlines to the two rounds were last extended in September by about two months to November 15.

The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to more than a decade in prison
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”

British comedian and Hollywood star Russell Brand was sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault by the Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday (November 9, 2026). Brand, 51, was found guilty on Thursday (November 5, 2026) by the court of rape and three counts of sexual assault and not guilty on three other counts. He was charged in relation to a total of seven crimes. His crimes were committed between 2004 and 2009. The court found him guilty of raping a woman in 2009 at his home, after meeting her at a comedy show in the Hammersmith neighbourhood of London. Brand has the possibility of being released in about seven years subject to conditions, the judge said.

“The consequences of what happened have affected almost every aspect of my life. Even now, I continue to experience anxiety, difficulties with trust, reduced confidence and the lasting effects of trauma,” the woman who was raped said on Monday (November 9, 2026) at the sentencing.
One of his victims said she was in “shock and turmoil” and did not “have any respect” for herself as a result of the attack on her. The judge referred to Brand as a “sexual predator”.

Brand had argued during the trial that while his past behaviour had been “wrong”, he had never forced himself on anybody. The actor was formerly a left-wing activist. In the early years of the current decade, he moved to the right, becoming skeptical of vaccines and the origins of COVID-19, building bonds with big names in U.S. President Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, including the President’s son, Donald Trump Jr., tech billionaire Elon Musk , commentators Alex Jones and Tucker Carlson, as well as Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the U.S. Health Secretary. In September, Brand participated in a video call event for the MAHA, Make America Healthy Again, movement, which is headed by Mr. Kennedy Jr. Brand converted to Christianity more recently and was baptized in the Thames in 2024.

articles.title: PM Modi speaks to Ukrainian President Zelenskyy on Kyiv-Moscow conflict, bilateral relations
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Modi, on Monday (November 9, 2026), spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict and bilateral relations between Delhi and Kyiv.

According to the PMO, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments in the ongoing conflict on the telephone call. PM Modi reaffirmed India’s “human-centric approach” and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to the peaceful resolution of the conflict.

“We are actively preparing on every item on the agenda for the meeting in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine has always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate,” President Zelenskyy posted on X regarding the talk. “It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end.”

Mr. Zelenskyy said that food security could be one of the areas of discussion. “We discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” he said.
The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors.

“Glad to have had a productive telephone conversation with President Zelenskyy. We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties,“ PM Modi said on X. “I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace. Reiterated India’s firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution.”

Meanwhile, Minister of External Affairs S. Jaishankar spoke this evening with Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of Russia. “Our conversation focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives,” the MEA posted on X.

Prime Minister Modi, on Monday (November 9, 2026), spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict and bilateral relations between Delhi and Kyiv.

According to the PMO, President Zelenskyy shared his perspective on recent developments in the ongoing conflict on the telephone call. PM Modi reaffirmed India’s “human-centric approach” and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to the peaceful resolution of the conflict.

“We are actively preparing on every item on the agenda for the meeting in Abu Dhabi. Ukraine has always taken a constructive approach, and Russia must show the same readiness to de-escalate,” President Zelenskyy posted on X regarding the talk. “It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end.”

Mr. Zelenskyy said that food security could be one of the areas of discussion. “We discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” he said.

The two leaders also discussed measures to further strengthen India-Ukraine bilateral cooperation in various sectors.

“Glad to have had a productive telephone conversation with President Zelenskyy. We reviewed our wide-ranging bilateral cooperation and agreed to further strengthen India-Ukraine ties,“ PM Modi said on X. “I thanked President Zelenskyy for sharing his perspectives on the ongoing conflict, its humanitarian aspects and various efforts to restore peace. Reiterated India’s firm commitment to contributing in every possible way towards a peaceful resolution.”

Meanwhile, Minister of External Affairs S. Jaishankar spoke this evening with Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of Russia. “Our conversation focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives,” the MEA posted on X.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Iran continues to at least partly block traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which has dented oil supplies out of the Gulf.
U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday (November 8, 2026) cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN that it was "highly unlikely" so long as talks progressed.
In recent weeks, Mr. Trump has threatened to renew strikes with U.S. media reports suggesting that hostilities could resume after the U.S. midterm elections this week.

"The answer is highly unlikely it's going to be necessary... I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don't know how hard I hit them," Mr. Trump said, while warning that any decision to resume hostilities "depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement."
Mr. Trump previously acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the stinging defeat that his Republican Party suffered in Tuesday's vote.

In the CNN interview on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting a peace deal on the United States' terms.
"They're a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation," Mr. Trump claimed. "They're withering away financially. We've hit them militarily. We could finish them off."

But earlier on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the Democratic Party's landslide victory was being assessed.

"For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone," Mr. Araghchi told state television. "We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward."

articles.title: Dhaka wants Hasina extradited under prisoner exchange
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasina seeks fresh passport, but Minister Humayun Kabir calls ousted leader a “terrorist” and dismisses request; no response from MEA, sources say denial of passport may complicate matter if India were to extradite Hasina

Hours after a legal team representing deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport for her, the Government of Bangladesh asserted on Monday (November 9, 2026) that Ms. Hasina can return to Bangladesh through an “acceptable prisoner exchange” programme governed by the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
Speaking to the media in Dhaka, the country’s Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir described Ms. Hasina as a “terrorist” who had fled to India after committing crimes.

A source in Dhaka told The Hindu that Ms. Hasina has requested the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, through a London-based legal firm, for a new passport and a National Identity Card. The official said the Ministry is verifying the letter and will take a final decision after internal consultations. Ms. Hasina’s passport was revoked soon after she escaped to India in August 2024 after an uprising toppled her government.

“Bangladesh will not issue a passport to any terrorist; there is no provision for such an action. Bangladesh will seek the return of Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner exchange process,” said Mr. Kabir, in response to questions from journalists regarding the request.

He noted that Ms. Hasina is a convict sentenced to death and has no legal or moral right to obtain a passport. Mr. Kabir said India should hand over the ousted Prime Minister under the extradition treaty. He added that Ms. Hasina and several of her colleagues from the Awami League are responsible for violent crimes and financial fraud, and need to be brought to justice.

The Ministry of External Affairs is yet to respond to Mr. Kabir’s remarks, but a source familiar with the Indian stance on the matter told The Hindu that the Bangladeshi position of not issuing a passport to Ms. Hasina will further complicate the matter, as a passport will be needed if India were to consider her extradition.

The Bangladeshi official, who spoke to The Hindu , said over the phone, “We have received an email from Matrix Chambers, a law firm in London, seeking a new passport for Sheikh Hasina. We are currently examining the contents of the letter and will take an appropriate step after internal consultation.”

However, the Press Secretary of the Bangladesh High Commission, Md. Saidur Rahman, said the Bangladesh authorities are “not sure if the request is genuine”. “There is no way for us to verify whether the request was actually made on behalf of Sheikh Hasina, as the email sent by the law firm did not include any authorisation letter or supporting documents proving that the firm was authorised by her to make such a request,” he said.

articles.title: Commercial cultivation within forest land not protected under FRA, 2006: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Says FRA protects forest-dwelling communities dependent on forests for generations, not commercial cultivators and plantation owners
The Supreme Court has made it clear that commercial crop cultivation within reserve forest areas is not protected under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006.

The court has distinguished commercial cultivators and plantation owners from forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, who have lived in forests for generations and depend on them for livelihood. Their rights are protected under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, commonly known as the FRA.
A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta recorded the court’s view in an order concerning extensive silk cotton cultivation within the reserve forests of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve.

The court, in its November 6 order, directed the Central Empowered Committee to examine the Tamil Nadu government’s opinion that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. Presently, 3,637.83 hectares of the 5,072.64 hectares of forest land are under silk cotton cultivation.
However, the Bench made clear its prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton.

“What emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop… The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” the apex court noted.

“We are of the prima facie view that planned or promoted cultivation of a commercial crop inside the forest areas is completely impermissible, as no such right is recognised under the FRA, 2006. The Act recognises the right of forest dwellers to collect, use and dispose of minor forest produce in accordance with Section 3(1)(c). The cultivation of a commercial crop cannot, therefore, be recognised as a forest right so as to justify occupation or continued presence within the forest area,” the Bench said.
ALSO WATCH Will Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Siang dam protect India against China’s mega-dam? | Insight India
The court did not accept the Tamil Nadu government’s claim that the cultivation of silk cotton justified the presence of the cultivators in the forest area.
“If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change,” Justice Mehta, who authored the order, observed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change,” Justice Mehta, who authored the order, observed.

articles.title: At peak of air pollution on Deepavali night, data goes missing at several govt monitoring stations in Delhi
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: ‘When the hourly PM2.5 data is missing, it will artificially lower the Air Quality Index, showing better air quality, when the actual air quality is worse,’ Manoj Kumar, analyst, Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air said

As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 150-200 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, but fell through the early morning hours of Monday (November 9, 2026) due to better weather conditions, show official data.

At the peak of pollution , following the bursting of firecrackers on Sunday night (November 8), crucial air quality data were missing from several monitoring stations managed by government authorities. Experts say missing data on peak values of air pollution will artificially show better air quality than the reality.
Though the Supreme Court allowed only green firecrackers during fixed windows on November 7 and 8, traditional firecrackers, which are more polluting, were also available in the markets of Delhi .

As per the Delhi government’s Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data, the level of PM2.5 (a major pollution) in Patparganj of East Delhi was 2,597 micrograms per cubic metre at 1 a.m. on Monday — about 173.13 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic metre for a 24-hour period.

Similarly, the level of PM2.5 in NSUT West Campus was 3,008.4 micrograms per cubic metre at 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) — about 200.5 times the WHO permissible limit. PM2.5 (Particulate matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.

Gufran Beig, chair professor, National Institute of Advanced Studies, said though the air pollution spiked around 12 midnight on Sunday (November 8) to 5 a.m. on Monday (November 9) due to bursting of firecrackers on Deepavali, both wind direction and speed were very favourable for faster dispersion of air pollution.

“The wind direction was earlier north westerly, originating from stubble burning areas in Punjab and Haryana. articles.title: Chennai sees dozens of cracker-related eye injuries; doctors call for caution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The day may have been wet, but Chennaiites still went all out to bring in light and sparkles on Deepavali day, which fell on Sunday (November 8, 2026). While awareness about safety has increased, ophthalmologists in the city have once again called for caution and reiterated protective measures, as they have received dozens of cases of cracker-related injuries.
The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital received around 50 cases, with about 10 cases having to be admitted, a senior official said.

Over the Deepavali weekend, the emergency clinic at Sankara Nethralaya saw 45 cases of firecracker injuries at its main campus. Two underwent wound repair surgery, while two others were scheduled for surgery on Monday, November 9, according to T.S. Surendran, its chairman..
Chennai’s air quality deteriorates to ‘poor’ the morning after Deepavali
Poor response from residents to Chennai Corporation’s appeal for segregated collection of cracker waste

At Dr. Agarwals Eye Hospital, nearly 20 patients came in with cracker-related injuries, said S. Soundari, regional head, clinical services. One of these, she explained, was a very serious case that had been taken up for surgery. Another patient lit a firecracker, but it did not blast. He went near it to take a look, and it blasted in his face, injuring both eyes. The remaining injuries were mostly small, and would be treated medically, she said. Four cases involved children; the rest were adults, mostly in their 30s and 40s.

At Rajan Eye Care, about 15 patients have been seen over the past three days or so, said Mohan Rajan, chairman and medical director of the hospital. One patient had to undergo a surgery, while minor injuries were treated as outpatients.

Doctors have reiterated caution. Dr. Soundari called for wearing protective eye gear while bursting firecrackers, supervising children properly, and importantly, not trying to touch the eye or take objects out by oneself. “Come to a doctor immediately if there is an eye injury,” she stressed. Dr. Rajan noted that bystanders often got hurt and should be careful to maintain an adequate distance..

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Reservation / court / Caste / labour / government / Census 2027

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / government / politics / language / Delimitation / education / Governor / taxes and duties / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Bharatiya Janata Party

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Editorial Context: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ministers (government) / voting / Aadhaar / welfare / Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / Bihar / court / Citizenship / West Bengal / political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Census 2027
